summary: Senkyo Sakawa studied at Rissho University until 1965. In Buddhist studies, he served as a professor in the Department of Buddhist Studies at Rissho University and as a member (assistant professor) of the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra.

Senmyo Naniwa, a scholar of Buddhist studies, completed a PhD at Savitribai Phule Pune University and studied under Genjun Sasaki, Mohan G. Dhadphale, J. R. Joshi, and P. V. Bapat. He was a professor at Bukkyo University and researcher at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.
Sensho Kimura is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University from circa 1962 to 1971. He later served as a professor at Otani University from circa 1980 to 2008.

Sensho Murakami was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University, Toyo University, and under Ryobun, Yukitada Takeda, and Gokan Un'ei. He taught at Komazawa and Toyo universities and served as a professor at the University of Tokyo.

Seraphim Rose studied at San Diego High School, the University of Southern California, the California Institute of Integral Studies under Alan Watts, and UC Berkeley. Active in philosophy and religious studies, he held a post with the Russian Orthodox Patriarchal Parishes in the United States.

Sergey Oldenburg, a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, studied under Ivan Minayev at Saint Petersburg State University. He served as professor at Saint Petersburg State University, led the Imperial Academy of Sciences, and directed the Asiatic Museum.

Serinity Young was a scholar in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology who earned her PhD from Columbia University in 1990 under Alex Wayman and studied under Vidya Dehejia. She held posts at Southern Methodist University and the American Museum of Natural History.
Sesso Oda was a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied under and succeeded Zuigan Goto. He taught students including Sōkō Morinaga and Gary Snyder.

Seung-yeon Lee is a scholar in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He studied under doctoral supervisor Lee Sang-hae and has held posts at Sungkyunkwan University and the Gyeonggi Institute of Cultural Properties.

Seunghak Koh, a Buddhist studies scholar, earned an MA at Seoul National University and a PhD from UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr. in 2011. He has served as an appointed researcher at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

Seungsahn Haengwon was a religious studies and Buddhist studies figure who studied at Dongguk University and under Ko Bong Sunim, Keumbong, and Keum'oh. He founded the Kwan Um School of Zen in 1970 and taught numerous students.

Shailendra Bhandare is a scholar of Indology and history and archaeology. He has held positions as curator at the British Museum, fellow at the Fitzwilliam Museum and St Cross College, and assistant keeper of numismatics at the Ashmolean Museum.

Shaman Hatley, working in Indology and religious studies, studied at Goddard College and the University of Pennsylvania, where he completed his PhD in 2007. He taught at Concordia University and became chair of Asian studies at the University of Massachusetts Boston in 2015.
Shan Shan Zhao works in Buddhist studies and sinology. She earned a Master of Arts at McMaster University, studying under supervisor James A. Benn as well as Shayne Clarke and Mark Rowe.
Shanshan Jia is a scholar in Indology. She was a doctoral student in Indology at the University of Hamburg, studying under doctoral supervisor Harunaga Isaacson in 2015.

Shaoyong Ye is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who completed his doctoral studies at Peking University in 2009 under Qing Duan. He subsequently served as an associate professor at Peking University.
Sharon J. Roe is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. She earned her PhD at the California Institute of Integral Studies, where she studied under doctoral supervisor Steven D. Goodman.

Shashibhusan Dasgupta worked in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Brojomohun College, Scottish Church College, and the University of Calcutta, where he earned his MA and PhD and served as a lecturer from circa 1945 to 1964.

Shayne Clarke, an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar, studied at Bukkyo University, the University of Canterbury under Paul Harrison, and UCLA under Gregory Schopen. He served as an associate professor at McMaster University.

Shechen Gyaltsab was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under numerous masters, including Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye, Patrul Rinpoche, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He taught Dilgo Khyentse and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, among others.
